transcript:
In the drawing window, double-click to open the Previous Files folder.  
Locate the C, Simulation, Instability, Layered Patterns, and the Gizmo Tool.  
Find the C, Simulation, Instability, Layered Patterns, and the Gizmo Tool in the double-click window of either the 2D or 3D window.  
If the 3D window is not properly arranged, there is a high likelihood that the simulation will be unstable.  
Additionally, there must be enough space between the panel layers to prevent conflicts during simulation, so the panel needs to be rearranged.  
In the 2D window,  
select the 3D window panel.  
On the 3D window panel, right-click and select Rearrange 2D Arrangement from the menu.  
Choose to rearrange the position of the 3D panel.  
Use the positioning tool to arrange the layers between the 3D panels.  
Now, if you want to rearrange the layers, select the 3D panel.  
Use the positioning tool to move the layers from one 3D panel to another.  
Turn on the fire simulation to observe the effect after adjustment  
and adjust the length according to the output.  
I will discuss it again after spreading.  
Now, it remains to install the todos.  
It is now working  
better than it was before.

chunks.content: ## Accessing and Preparing Multi-layer Garment Panels for Simulation This section explains how to locate and arrange multi-layer garment panels within CLO’s simulation environment, focusing on the use of the Previous Files folder, the Gizmo Tool, and the importance of proper panel spacing to avoid simulation instability. To begin, open the Previous Files folder by double-clicking in the drawing window. Locate the files related to simulation instability and layered patterns, as well as the Gizmo Tool, which is essential for manipulating garment panels. Access these elements through either the 2D or 3D window by double-clicking. It is important to note that an improperly arranged 3D window often causes simulation instability. Ensuring there is adequate space between panel layers is critical to prevent conflicts during simulation. Therefore, panel layers must be rearranged if necessary to maintain sufficient spacing. ## Rearranging Panel Layers Using the 2D and 3D Windows This section details the procedure for rearranging multi-layer garment panels using the 2D and 3D windows and the positioning tools within CLO, emphasizing how to improve simulation stability. Start by selecting the garment panel in the 2D window that corresponds to the 3D panel you want to adjust. In the 3D window, right-click on the panel and select “Rearrange 2D Arrangement” from the contextual menu. This option allows you to adjust the placement of the 3D panel within the workspace. Use the positioning tool to organize and space the layers between the 3D panels appropriately. You can move individual layers from one 3D panel to another if re-layering is required to reduce conflicts during simulation. ## Testing and Fine-tuning Simulation Stability This section covers how to verify the effect of panel rearrangement on simulation stability using CLO’s simulation tools and how to adjust layer lengths for optimal results. After rearranging the panels, activate the simulation to observe how the adjustments affect garment behavior. Pay close attention to any instability or collisions between layers. Adjust the length and positioning of garment panels as needed based on the simulation output. Iteratively refine these adjustments to achieve smoother and more stable simulation results. The process of rearrangement and testing should continue until the simulation performs better than the initial unstable state.
